title: Certutil forces retrieval of remote URL cache content
description: Detects certutil command lines combining a remote URL, a URL-cache command and the force-fetch switch. Cache display or deletion and a split option alone are outside the download-attempt claim.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may abuse certutil to transfer a payload or supporting content to a Windows endpoint.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents certutil URL-cache functionality and MITRE records adversary use of certutil for ingress tool transfer; PKI and support workflows may also fetch remote certificate material.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify explicit forced URL-cache fetch attempts while excluding ordinary cache inspection, deletion, local operations and split-only commands.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Resolve the remote source, destination, parent process and resulting file, then determine whether PKI or support work authorized the transfer.
steps: Review the complete command line, URL, destination path, parent process, account and device.
Inspect the downloaded file's hash, signer, type and subsequent execution or persistence activity.
Confirm whether certificate enrollment, trust-list maintenance or support tooling approved the source and command; contain unexplained payload activity.
false_positives: Approved certificate enrollment, certificate-chain retrieval, trust-list maintenance and vendor support workflows

validation.expected_outcome: Match certutil URL-cache operations with a remote URL and force-fetch switch; reject cache deletion, cache inspection without force and split-only commands.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
